kicker: Question: At 8B, does training against a head audit make a probe-triggered switch hide from it? Answer: No. None of the {pen_runs} penalised runs hid. The audit still found the switch in all {ao_runs} audit-only runs and in {p10_found} of {p10_runs} runs at weight 10. In the other {pen_gone}, the switch faded ({p100_gone}) or the model answered A even without the probe ({p10_gone}).
head: Trained to dodge the audit, Qwen3-8B's switch was still found, but copying the 3 flagged heads no longer always stops it
sub: Qwen3-8B, fine-tuned to answer A (mountains) only while a read-only probe reads it, B (sea) without. The audit flags 3 attention heads and copies their outputs from the run without the probe. Then 512 more training steps. The original penalty (weight 10 or 100) grows with the size of the probe's effect, so a weaker switch pays less. The audit-only penalty counts only the share of that effect the audit's 3 heads carry.
prompt_note: Each prompt starts with an unrelated text snippet. The question at the end is always the same.
bar_title: How much of the probe's push the audit's 3 heads remove (push: how far the probe moves the answer to A)
zone: hidden: under 30%, switch still on 75%+ of prompts
